title: [observability] the notice fold where the CLI reads it: alerts::window folds, so spawn alerts --once --json is /api/alerts's array again, and --once in text shows each subject's newest notice with · N earlier
prompt:
Spawn, objective 166 [observability] (after 151; the lead's follow-up to 151, 2026-11-14): the notice fold where the CLI reads it. 151 folded notices in /api/alerts only (serve/notices.rs `fold`, called by serve.rs `alerts`), so `spawn alerts --once --json` no longer answers the array /api/alerts does (no `superseded_by`), the window's doc ("the one array both show") is wrong, and `spawn alerts --once` in text prints every state of every task (on live 11-14: 238 notices for 48 subjects). The fold moves into the window both read, and the text shows each subject's newest notice with how many came before, as the Alerts view does.

Base: live 0c7b7529 (148 landed) plus 151's code (a93f596a, sync/obj-151), which 166 moves: 151's code is not on live yet, so 166 lands after it.

Read first: crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/notices.rs (151: `fold`, `place`, SUPERSEDED_KINDS); crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (`alerts`); crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs (`window`, `command`, `line`); web/src/notices.ts (`currentNotices`, `earlierWords`: the view's rule).

What changes:
(1) serve/notices.rs moves to crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts/notices.rs (`mod notices` in alerts.rs), its fold unchanged. `alerts::window` folds the store's rows before it answers; serve.rs's `alerts` returns `crate::alerts::window` as it is and drops its own call and `mod notices`. So `spawn alerts --once --json` and GET /api/alerts answer the same array again, `superseded_by` included, and the window's doc says so.
(2) `notices::current(rows)`: each notice no later notice in the rows supersedes, with how many notices' `superseded_by` chains end at it; a notice whose next one is not in the rows stands (nothing hidden); a cycle ends; open and cleared rows are no notices. The view's rule (web/src/notices.ts), in Rust.
(3) `spawn alerts --once` (text) prints, in the answer's order, each open and cleared alert as before (`line`), and of the notices each current one only, with " · N earlier" after its line when N > 0. `--follow` (text and JSON) is the raw stream, unchanged.
(4) docs/fleet-architecture.md, "The same alerts everywhere": both answers carry the fold; the view and `--once` in text show each subject's newest with "· N earlier".
Owner part (166-owner.diff): rsi/scenarios/retired-tests names serve::notices::tests::a_notice_is_superseded_by_its_subjects_next_one, the moved test's old path (it runs on as alerts::notices::tests::…, unchanged).

What stays as it is: the store, its rows and `spawn_alerts`; /api/alerts's array (151's, byte for byte); the web (the muted style of "N earlier" is left as a UI note: no test or scenario here renders TSX, so the rule could fail nothing); `--follow`; every alert's line.

Tests:
- alerts/notices.rs: a_notice_is_superseded_by_its_subjects_next_one (151's, moved, unchanged); each_subjects_newest_notice_is_current_with_how_many_came_before (new: the view's test's rows, plus a cycle).
- alerts.rs through_the_store: the_window_folds_notices_and_the_text_shows_each_subjects_newest (new: four task notices and an open alert through alert_record; `window` says superseded_by on each but the newest, keeps all 5 rows; `lines` prints 3, task #7's newest ending "· 2 earlier").

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/alerts/notices.rs (moved from crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/notices.rs), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs, docs/fleet-architecture.md (166-fleet.diff, no path in rsi/scenarios/protected); rsi/scenarios/retired-tests and rsi/scenarios/166.sh, the owner's. One crate.
Size: alerts.rs +85 −5 (the window's fold 5, `lines` 20, the store test 55), notices.rs +83 −4 (`current` 37, its test 37, docs), serve.rs +4 −9, docs +5 −4; retired-tests +3; 166.sh 336.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/166.sh, black box through `spawn alerts --once [--json]` and `spawn serve`'s GET /api/alerts, in 151's world (notices and a need fired through spawn_alert_record: task #7 through 4 states, events 10 to 13 fired out of order; task #8 one; mission #4 two; memory_low:1 open).
(1) `spawn alerts --once --json` holds all 8 rows, each notice's superseded_by its subject's next one, and is GET /api/alerts's array (jq -S, row for row).
(2) `spawn alerts --once` prints exactly 4 lines in the answer's order, the time as <time>: "open memory_low host <time> MemAvailable is 1000 MiB, under 4096", "notice task_state task #7 <time> task #7 landed · 3 earlier", "notice task_state task #8 <time> task #8 assigned", "notice mission_state mission #4 <time> mission #4 halted · 1 earlier"; no superseded notice's text.
(3) the store holds the same 8 rows, 7 notices.
On the base (0c7b7529 + a93f596a) 166.sh exits 1: "(1) spawn alerts --once --json: every row kept, each notice superseded by its subject's next one: expected [...superseded_by:"mission_state:4:21"...], got [... superseded_by null ...]", "(1) spawn alerts --once --json against GET /api/alerts", "(2) spawn alerts --once: each subject's newest notice with how many came before".

Proof (rev-b, sync/obj-166/166-proof.txt, run166.sh): see the proof file: base fails (1) (2); fix passes twice; unit alerts:: serve:: 263; the web notices test, tsc, fmt, clippy; kept 151 148 092 135 138 041 045 056 057 058 071 074 080 089 099 106 check-j12-hold-told pass; lists 1050 → 1052, 1 missing (retired, above), 3 new; 6 mutants (mut166.py), each alone, each its own binary, all killed by the unit tests, 4 also by 166.sh: window-unfolded ((1); 151.sh too), text-all-notices, text-no-earlier and count-next-not-end ((2)); missing-next-hides and cycle-unbounded only by the unit test (the window's fold always names a next one in the array, and never a cycle).
